newsitem.title: LATVIA: Unibanka drops on Latvia bourse on state sale news.
newsitem.headline: Unibanka drops on Latvia bourse on state sale news.

text.p: Latvia's sagging bourse was bitten by another bear on Friday as official list leader Unibanka eased on news that the state would shed one million of its shares in the bank.
But dealers took some heart from the performance of other blue chip stocks. Three of the other five official list stocks gained and one held steady, albeit in very light trade.

Dealers said Unibanka's reduced price could attract buyers and stimulate activity on the listless bourse, which has been hit hard by the summer lull and competition from privatisation vouchers and the relatively low-risk local debt market.
Volume remained low with only 43,000 lats worth of trade registered. The bourse index slipped 5.71 points to 380.07 while the Rietumu index lost 1.18 percent to 151.3.

Unibanka eased 3.3 percent to 3.25 lats as the market digested a Latvian Privatisation Agency announcement that it planned to auction one million of the state's shares in the bank at a minimum price of 3.25 lats on July 28.
Dealers expected the bank to fall further.
"Unibanka will certainly fall further until the auction...one million shares is a lot in Latvia's market," said one dealer.
"But a cheaper Unibanka should bring more investors to the market and that will help increase volumes," he added.
